transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because of the contract work, mostly. The environmental modeling one. I’ve been doing this kind of math for years, and I know what a normal version-control mix-up looks like, but this is… different.

People on that project are tracking my revisions, I’m pretty sure. And then errors show up in the datasets, but not in a way that makes sense. It’s like they’re being planted so it looks like I can’t manage the work, or can’t lead the team. My wife says I’m reading too much into it, and one of the junior analysts said it’s probably just file conflicts, but I’ve seen enough patterns in data to know when something isn’t random.
Have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?

I don’t know. I mean, not like… seeing a person standing there that nobody else sees, if that’s what you mean. Hearing things, I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. Sometimes you hear something in a building and people act like it’s nothing, but buildings make noise, computers make noise, air systems hum—especially in the older labs, the vents were terrible.

So, no, I don’t think that’s the main issue. The issue is the way the files change and then everyone wants to say it’s just normal errors. That’s what bothers me.
Have there been times lately when you felt unusually energized or driven, more than is normal for you?

Unusually energized… I don’t know if I’d call it that. I’ve always had stretches where I get very focused, especially if there’s a problem in the numbers. That’s just how the work goes—you pull one thread and then there are six more, and before you know it you’re comparing outputs from three versions ago.

But more than normal? I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it as energy so much as trying to keep up with what’s happening. My wife might say I get locked in, but that’s different than being… whatever you mean by unusually energized.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?

I don’t think so. I mean, there are times when the house is quiet and you hear something—pipes, the refrigerator cycling, a neighbor’s TV maybe—and you wonder for a second. But voices, like someone talking to me when nobody’s there… I haven’t really noticed that. The file issues are more what I keep coming back to.
Lately, have you felt unusually cheerful, high, or euphoric for no clear reason?

Cheerful? No, I wouldn’t say that exactly. I mean, I have good moments like anyone, if I solve something or if the weather’s decent and I can get out for a walk, but “euphoric” sounds… dramatic.

Lately it’s more been trying to keep things straight. People use words like “happy” in a very broad way, you know—my wife will say, “You seem better today,” but that could just mean I slept a little or I’m not talking about work files at breakfast. So no, I haven’t noticed feeling high for no reason.
When did you first start feeling that people were tracking your revisions or planting errors in the files?

I think… it’s been about two months that I’ve been pretty sure of it. Before that there were little things, you know, odd changes in the revisions, numbers not lining up the way they should, but I could still explain it as a mistake or a bad merge or someone being careless.

But the certainty that people on the project are tracking what I change and putting errors in there—yeah, that’s really been there for the last couple of months. It’s hard to pin down the exact day, because with files you’re always going back and forth, and sometimes an old version looks new if the timestamp’s been handled wrong… but about two months.
Lately, have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling okay the next day?

Less sleep and still okay? I’m not sure I’d put it that way. My sleep’s been… ordinary for me, I guess. Some nights I’m up thinking, but that happens if I’ve had too much coffee or if I’m trying to remember whether I closed a document properly, and then you start thinking about where the backup went—sorry.

But no, I haven’t noticed needing, like, only a couple hours and then feeling great the next day. Usually if I don’t sleep enough, I feel it.
Have you had the feeling that other people can somehow know your thoughts as you are thinking them?

Not exactly like they can hear the words in my head, no. It’s more… they seem to know what I’m going to change in the files, or they’re watching the revisions close enough that it amounts to the same thing.

That environmental modeling contract—every time I clean up a dataset or correct something, some new error shows up, and then it looks like I’m the one who can’t manage the work. My wife says it’s probably version-control issues, and the junior analysts say that too, but they would say that if they didn’t want to look too closely. So, thoughts, I don’t know… but my work, my decisions, yes, they seem to know those.
Before these concerns started, had you had any recent illness, head injury, seizure, or started any new medication?

I don’t think so… I mean, not that I can point to. I didn’t hit my head or anything like that that I remember. No seizure, unless you mean something very small that a person wouldn’t know about, but I haven’t had anything obvious.

Illness… I get the usual aches and being tired, especially if I’ve been sitting at the computer too long, and sometimes you think it’s a cold and it’s really just the air in the office, those vents are terrible. But nothing big before this started. And medication, I don’t think there was anything new. I’d have to look at the bottles at home to be exact, but nothing comes to mind.
Have these experiences been going on for longer than three months?

Longer than three months? No, I don’t think so. The thing with the project—people tracking my revisions, the errors showing up like they’ve been put there—that’s been… maybe about two months now.

It feels longer because every file has its own history, you know, and then you start going back through old versions and it’s like time stretches out. But if you mean when I became sure something was going on, I’d say around two months.
Since these concerns began, has your ability to do your job dropped noticeably?

Yes… I mean, noticeably, yes. I don’t like saying it that way because I’ve done this kind of work for years, and usually I’m the one people come to when the model won’t behave.

But I’ve fallen behind on the deliverables, far enough that the firm started handing pieces of the contract to other people. And the junior analysts—I’m supposed to be supervising them, but lately I’m not much help. I get stuck checking things, going back through files, and then suddenly half the day is gone.

At home it’s… not great either. I mostly keep to myself. My wife has to push me to keep up with basic things, routines, meals, getting moving. I know that sounds simple, but it all gets tangled together.
Have people told you lately that you seem emotionally flat or less expressive than usual?

Yeah… my wife has said something like that. Not in those exact words maybe, but that I’m just kind of… blank, or not reacting.

I can sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage where the telescope is, and it’s still got the cover on it. Which is stupid, because I used to like that. Astronomy nights, hiking, helping the younger analysts work through a model—those things used to get me going. Now I know I should start something, call someone, uncover the telescope, whatever, but there’s just no pull to do it.

It’s not that I’m trying to be cold. I just don’t seem to have much showing on my face, or much to say.
Have other people told you lately that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

Hard to follow? I don’t… I’m not sure anyone has said it like that. My wife sometimes asks me to slow down, but that might just be because I’m explaining the file structure, and honestly the way those revisions branch, it’s not simple—people think there’s one version, but there’s the saved copy, the emailed copy, the one with comments hidden…

Sorry. I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I haven’t been told directly that I’m jumping around, no.
Have you found yourself talking much less than usual lately?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t really start conversations much anymore.

I can sit at my desk for hours, or out in the garage with the telescope still covered, and I’ll think, you know, I used to go to astronomy nights, used to talk with people about what we were looking at. Or with the younger analysts, I’d walk them through a model and actually enjoy explaining it. Hiking too, there was always something to say about the trail or the weather or… whatever.

Now I just don’t feel much pull to start. Even if someone’s around, I mostly let it go quiet. It’s not that I’m trying to ignore anyone. It just feels like too much effort to begin talking.
Have you heard a voice speaking to you when no one else was there?

I don’t think so. I mean… not like a person standing in the room talking to me.

Sometimes if the house is quiet, I’ll think I heard something, but then it’s the refrigerator kicking on, or the pipes, or a car outside. Our old garage makes noises too, especially near the telescope cabinet—wood settling, that kind of thing. I used to be able to tell exactly what was what, because I’d be out there more, checking the sky charts and—

Sorry. No, I haven’t really heard a voice speaking to me when nobody was there.
Since this started, have there been times when your thoughts or behavior changed very suddenly from one hour to the next?

From one hour to the next? I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I notice it like a switch flipping.

Some days I’m more… stuck, I guess, and other times I can get moving, but that might be normal. Like if I’m trying to sort through old work files, I can spend an hour just naming folders the right way, because if the labels aren’t right later you can’t trust the whole thing, and then suddenly I realize I haven’t actually done what I meant to do.

But sudden changes in my thoughts or behavior, hour by hour… I’m not sure. I haven’t really been tracking it that closely.
Have you felt that an outside force is putting thoughts into your mind?

I don’t know if it’s like… an outside force putting thoughts into my mind exactly.

But I do think something is being done from outside, yes. The people from that environmental modeling contract—I’m pretty sure they’ve been tracking my revisions. Not just watching, but putting errors into the datasets, little things that make it look like I’m the one who can’t manage the work anymore.

My wife says it’s probably version-control problems, and the junior analysts say that too, but they don’t understand how these models are structured. One wrong input and the whole projection shifts, like with weather patterns when you think it’s just a small pressure change and then—

Sorry. So, no, not thoughts placed in my head maybe. But I do feel like they’re interfering, making it look like my judgment is failing.
Did these beliefs about people tracking your revisions and planting errors come on very suddenly?

No, not like all at once in one hour. It sort of built up as I kept seeing the same kinds of mistakes in the files, the revisions not matching what I’d done.

I’m here because I’m pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting errors in the datasets to make it look like I can’t lead the work. My wife keeps saying it’s just version-control mistakes, and the junior analysts say that too, but they don’t see the pattern the way I do. It’s like when you’re doing a model and one tiny input keeps drifting—people think it’s random until the whole thing points somewhere else.
Have you had the feeling that thoughts are being taken out of your mind?

Thoughts taken out? I’m not sure I’d put it that way. Sometimes I lose track of what I was thinking, but that happens when you’re trying to keep too many variables in your head at once.

It’s like when I’m looking at a model and I know there was a step I meant to check, and then I’m staring at the screen thinking, wait, what was the sequence again? But I don’t know if that means something was taken out of my mind. That sounds… different. I haven’t really noticed it like that.
Since these experiences began, have there been any days when the beliefs about people tampering with your work went away completely?

No, not really completely. I mean, there are times I’m distracted by other things—making coffee, fixing something in the house, that sort of thing—but if I sit back down and look at the files, it’s still there.

I’m pretty sure those people on the environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting errors in the datasets. That doesn’t just vanish because my wife says it’s version-control mistakes, or because the junior analysts shrug it off. They don’t see the pattern. It’s like… well, with models, you can miss the drift for a long time if you’re only looking at one variable. So no, I wouldn’t say there have been days where it went away completely.
